papers.title: EXPRESS: Biological Age and its Value to Marketing Theory and Practice
papers.authors: Steven D. Shaw, Remi Daviet, Gideon Nave
papers.abstract: Aging has profound effects on how we consume, yet marketers often simplify aging to the mere passage of time (chronological age; ChronAge), overlooking biological and psychological aspects and meaningful variation within ChronAge segments. This paper highlights the need for multidimensional approaches to studying aging consumers and pioneers a framework integrating biological aging into consumer behavior theory. It introduces a measure of biological age (BioAge), derived from epigenetic data, to marketing. Using Health and Retirement Study data, the analyses demonstrate that BioAge captures distinct aspects of aging, not reflected in ChronAge, and improves prediction of consumer activities and spending. BioAge is most useful in domains where functional capacity, energy, cognition, and health-related constraints shape engagement, including technology use, social and physical activity, and discretionary entertainment spending, and is limited in more routinized or necessity-based domains. The analyses further show that BioAge mediates the impact of time on consumer behavior through objective physiological pathways, including chronic disease, cognitive functioning, and physical vitality, rather than subjective perceptions of health. The paper concludes with implications and best practices, including how BioAge can improve segmentation and customer lifetime value optimization, and the ethical and legal challenges of its use in research and practice.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Causal Alignment: Augmenting Language Models with A/B Tests
papers.authors: Panagiotis Angelopoulos, Kevin Lee, Sanjog Misra
papers.abstract:
We develop a framework for improving the effectiveness of marketing communications by aligning a language model to the causal signal in A/B tests. The core idea is that randomized experiments reveal not just which content performs best, but directions of improvement that can serve as supervision for a generative model. Using within-experiment comparisons, we fine-tune a language model to create an
                    improver
                    architecture that transforms lower-performing content into higher-performing content. The resulting model can be composed with any baseline decision-maker, e.g. a human expert, to suggest improvements to new content. We validate our framework through a large-scale field experiment in email marketing spanning 36 new campaigns and 283 million impressions. Subject lines improved by our aligned model achieve click-through rates 32% higher than those from unassisted human experts, while a general-purpose language model with 30 times as many parameters as our fine-tuned model does not improve outcomes. This suggests that alignment to experimental data adds value beyond model capabilities alone. Our findings provide the first field evidence that aligning language models to A/B tests improves outcomes in real marketing campaigns and show that integrating AI with experimentation can train systems that make better future decisions.

papers.title: The Digital Journey of Health Insurance Marketing: Narrative Ads and Product Page Design
papers.authors: Yin Bai, Rui Wang, Xingyao Ren, Rajdeep Grewal
papers.abstract:
Selling health insurance through digital advertising is fundamentally different from selling most consumer products online: health insurance protects against abstract future risks, and regulatory constraints prohibit transactions from closing on third-party platforms, forcing consumers to transition from the ad platform to the insurer’s own product page. We examine how aligning narrative ad content with product page design sustains persuasion across this mandatory handoff. In a randomized field experiment with a leading Chinese insurer on Douyin, we study 335 ads that generated nearly 17 million impressions and 777,412 click-throughs. Users who clicked were randomly routed to either a fact-based product page or one incorporating a customer experience exemplar. Purchase conversion rises most when narrative ads are paired with the exemplar page, increasing from 1.51% to 2.05%, implying roughly 8,400 additional policies per month at campaign scale. Neither element is effective in isolation. A causal mediation analysis confirms that sustained engagement on the product page accounts for more than 80% of the total effect. To address algorithm-driven selection in ad delivery and self-selection into clicking, we employ a sequential endogeneity correction strategy and confirm robustness with causal forests. Aligning ad design with product page design significantly improves conversion in regulated digital markets.
